notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found for status 38, CLOSE WITH LOCK or the being-opened mode). §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR26 (Amendment 2): "If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, the physical file is not affected and the following actions take place in the following order": a, "A value is placed in the I-O status associated with file-name to indicate the condition that caused the OPEN statement to be unsuccessful."; b, "Any applicable USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure is executed." Implemented at 85 with no edition arm: EmitOpen emits, per file-name, the runtime OPEN, the store of the FILE STATUS item and then EmitUseHook, so the status is placed before the procedure runs and the procedure sees it; the hook's selector (EmitScopeTiers) takes the file-name procedure first and otherwise switches on FileRegistry.OpenModeOf, the mode the file is open in or was being opened in, which FileConnector.OpenOnce records for a failed open. The file is not affected: RefusedAsAlreadyOpen answers 41 before anything touches the open connector, and SequentialConnector.OpenCore returns 35 before it creates or truncates. Probed at --std 85: 35 (INPUT, I-O and EXTEND of an absent file: none created), 37 (OUTPUT, I-O and EXTEND of a read-only file: content unchanged), 30 (OUTPUT into a missing directory) and 41 (OUTPUT of a file open INPUT: its records still read) each place the status, run the applicable procedure, by file-name or by open mode, and continue at the next statement; in one OPEN INPUT naming three absent files the procedure runs once for each file-name, in order. Not implemented: the open-mode procedures for status 38. The closed-with-lock arm of SharedOpenAttempt sets 38 and returns before FileConnector.Open, so the attempted mode is never recorded; the CLOSE left the connector with no known mode, OpenModeView answers -1, and the selector finds no INPUT, OUTPUT, I-O or EXTEND procedure. An OPEN of a file closed WITH LOCK therefore runs a file-name procedure (probed: USE ... ON F runs with 38) but none of the four mode procedures, which §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR5 makes applicable to a file "in the process of being opened" in that mode; with no FILE STATUS clause the run unit then ends abnormally with a message saying no USE procedure applies. The arm is the registry's, shared by all organizations and editions that accept CLOSE WITH LOCK: probed, an indexed and a relative file at 85 and the sequential repro at --std 2002 and 2014 behave the same, so the Relative and Indexed modules' unsuccessful-OPEN rules carry the same finding. The witness covers 35 and 41 with file-name procedures only.

next.reason: 1985 (1993 amendment): an unsuccessful OPEN leaves 'the physical file' unaffected, then 'a. A value is placed in the I-O status', then 'b. Any applicable USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure is executed.' §2023:14.9.27.4 GR25 keeps 'the file is not affected', a) the I-O status, and d) 'Any applicable USE FOR EXCEPTION or USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure is executed', but adds cases: b) 'If it is enabled, the level-3 EC-I-O exception condition ... is set to exist', and c) an OPEN in an exception-checking PERFORM with an applicable WHEN phrase continues at that WHEN phrase and 'No applicable USE declarative is executed'. §2023:14.9.49.4 GR6 runs USE procedures only when the statement is outside an exception-checking PERFORM or no WHEN matched. Those programs (>>TURN, exception-checking PERFORM, USE FOR EXCEPTION) are accepted by 2023 and refused by 1985, and for them the result differs: a case added, so CHANGED. §2023:14.9.27.4 GR1 restates the I-O status update.
